builders.angle: GIVE A PROP AN INTERIOR. Fix 1 is the whole cause and it is yours: shapeField() returns a 2D coverage mask and the fragment shader builds its normal from the COVERAGE GRADIENT alone, so every prop in this game is a rounded slab with material noise on it -- which is exactly what an award statuette is. Round 8 solved this for the WALL by drawing subjects into RELIEF instead of colour, so they inherited recess occlusion, ink in their hollows and a lip on their crests. Props never got it. Build the companion relief field, author it in metres off vSize the way wallH does, derive N from coverage AND relief, and let mmDrawn ink the interior lines. Then prove it on the statue (used by the Ballroom, Graveyard, Crypt and Heart, so it pays four times): brow, nose and chin, vertical drapery channels, a plinth moulding, marble with a vein and a chipped edge. Remember marks on a prop must be DARK -- it already sits at its luminance ceiling, and a highlight added as a highlight does nothing on screen.

NOTHING IN THE GREENHOUSE LOOKS LIKE PLANTS. Fix 2a is yours and it is the first thing Josh named. Its prop SET is already right -- plants, shrubs, a lamp post, a column, thirty of them on a terrace -- so this is purely drawing, and round 8 attacked the silhouette three times and stopped there. The silhouette is not the problem, the interior is: one rounded-slab normal across a whole frond mass is the blob. A pot needs a rim that oversails, a belly, a foot, visible soil and a saucer; a leaf needs its own midrib as relief so it catches light on one side and loses it on the other, plus a curl so they do not all face the camera; a leaf crossing in front of another must be DARKER where it covers it; the ragged edge belongs at leaf scale, not mass scale; and a neglected glasshouse has a few dead fronds. Then do the Hedge Maze, which shares the foliage material and reads as mossy sarcophagi -- its three recorded failure modes are in fix 2a, and check anything you add against masonry first, because a hollow all the way round every clump is how a dry stone wall reads.

THE BALLROOM IS OCCUPIED BY OSCAR AWARDS, and that is a CONTENT failure before it is a drawing one. Fix 2b is yours. Thirty props on a colonnade layout led by a tall narrow statue is literally a row of award statuettes, in a room called The Ballroom and Velvet Suites whose own wall subject is already `mirrors`. A ballroom has pier mirrors and their frames, gilt chairs and settles round the walls, chandeliers, candelabra, a piano, a curtained dais. Change what is IN the room, add the silhouettes it needs and does not have, and cut the statues back or out. Then audit the other sixteen prop sets against fix 4's table the same way -- an armchair and a bookcase in the kennels, a headstone in a hedge maze -- and say in notes_for_merger which rooms you judged fine and why. Twenty silhouettes cover seventeen rooms, so a MISSING object type is a legitimate finding and worth adding when it is the difference between a room making sense and not.
